newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP could raise interest rates - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP could raise interest rates - paper.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland may raise interest rates to avoid a banking crisis after the recent boom in credit action, the Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted the central bank president as saying.
The paper said Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz was speaking at a meeting with journalists on Wednesday in Washington at a annual International Monetary Fund/World Bank meeting.
"The recent rise in credit action by Polish banks may cause a banking crisis and an interest rate rise," Gronkiewicz-Waltz was quoted as saying.
Lending to the non-financial sector rose 2.8 percent in the first 20 days of September after rising four percent in August.
Since the start of the year it has increased by 24 percent against a 17.4 percent rise in broad money supply.
The central bank last changed official interest rates, now at 25 and 22 percent, on July 16 by cuting them by one percent.
The NBP's spokeswoman Renata Wisniewska did not have any immediate comment.
